weight.method: Each entry point is bundled with `esbuild --bundle --minify --format=esm --platform=node` over a fixture that imports it and re-exports one symbol; the incumbent is bundled by the same command over the same fixture shape. Installed bytes are the package directory plus every production dependency, transitively — each dependency resolved from the directory of the package that depends on it, and deduplicated by resolved path, so a nested copy is counted where npm actually put it. Every top-level package is resolved from `benchmarks/`, whose package.json pins the versions — the workspace root has an older commander hoisted, and resolving from there would compare against the wrong package.

gate.why: a ratchet on what a user's bundle grows by; raising it is a decision, not a drift

the capability-parity stack for `burgee`: cac plus 3 package(s) a user of it installs to reach the same capability set — `cosmiconfig` for find and load a config file, and merge it under the flags; `exit-hook` for run cleanup on every path out, including a signal; `restore-cursor` for hand the terminal back with the cursor visible. Each addition is a package this repository publishes a graded drop-in for (`seniority/cosmiconfig`, `closeout/exit-hook`, `closeout/restore-cursor`), which is the rule that decides what may be in this stack

10452 bytes for `cac` alone, 97711 for the stack. Reported, never gated — a ceiling here would be a ceiling on somebody else's dependency tree. 5 of our capabilities have no incumbent to add and cost this stack nothing: `--schema`: the whole program as one JSON document; `--mcp`: the program as an MCP server over stdio; the `{ ok, data }` envelope on `--json`, on every command; agent detection, and the non-interactive floor that follows from it; option relations (`dependsOn`, `exclusive`) and Standard Schema validation
